correctness.rationale: The three exact Lanczos basis vectors give explicit physical coordinates by graph distance and a local triangle-adjusted degree. The symmetrically signed projected exponential has positive reduced coordinates by irreducible Metzler positivity. Its lowest Ritz mode has sign exactly the local margin, and the at-most-two-real-zeros property of three exponentials (with one zero fixed at time zero) proves both strict all-time positivity and a unique permanent sign transition. The rational witness satisfies 61-a1-a2=215528/138043>0, and Ritz nonnegativity finishes the counterexample. The checker reproduces 200 source/time tests and all critical exact fractions; finite tests are not used in place of infinite proof.

The closest published diagonal-mode Lanczos parity and two-step horizon results have incompatible objects and do not imply the all-graph three-step original-coordinate criterion. Exact theorem/alias/parameters searches of published records and recoverable local claims located no dominating result; incomplete indexing remains a risk.

value.rationale: Provides a general necessary-and-sufficient graph-local sign-safety test for a practical three-step matrix-exponential approximation, a one-way transition law rather than sampled signs, and a small rational diagnostic example. It separates physical positivity from standard projected semigroup positivity, norm-error guarantees and exact heat-kernel positivity; the classification applies to all finite weighted graphs rather than a contrived subfamily.
